metadata.title: Return Min and Max as a Tuple
metadata.description: Return two values from one function by packing them into a tuple.

instructions.main: Define `minmax(items)` so that it returns the smallest and largest values as a tuple — `minmax([3, 1, 2])` must return `(1, 3)`.
steps: Define `def minmax(items):` with exactly one parameter.
Return both values in ONE statement: `return min(items), max(items)` — the comma creates a tuple.
Do not print the values; return them.

hints.message: Define `def minmax(items):` and finish with `return min(items), max(items)`.
A list `[a, b]` is not a tuple — drop the brackets: `return min(items), max(items)`.
A function returns only once per call — a second `return` never runs. Return both values together as ONE tuple.

evaluation.feedback_on_all_pass: `minmax` returns the smallest and largest values as a tuple.

test_cases.feedback_on_fail: `minmax([3, 1, 2])` must return the tuple `(1, 3)` — use `return min(items), max(items)` in a single return statement.
Use a `return` statement inside `minmax` — do not print the result.
